name: Exception Handling Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for managing exceptions within FirstUK Bank, as defined in document EXCP-SOP-001. It is owned by the Head of Operations and intended for use by Operations Staff, Customer Service, and Compliance.

name: Head of Operations
description: The executive owner of the Exception Handling Guide responsible for the oversight and maintenance of the procedure.

name: Operations Staff
description: Internal staff within the Operations department who are part of the target audience for the exception handling procedures.
context: Audience | Operations Staff, Customer Service, Compliance

name: Customer Service
description: Staff members responsible for customer-facing interactions who are instructed on how to handle exceptions according to this guide.
context: Audience | Operations Staff, Customer Service, Compliance

name: Compliance
description: The compliance function responsible for ensuring that exception handling aligns with regulatory requirements and internal policy.
context: Audience | Operations Staff, Customer Service, Compliance

name: Operational Exception Resolution Process
description: A comprehensive procedure designed to identify, investigate, and resolve operational exceptions, including failed transactions, disputed transactions, and regulatory exceptions. The goal is to maintain regulatory compliance and ensure customer satisfaction.
context: Establish procedures for identifying, investigating, and resolving operational exceptions
failed transactions, disputed transactions, regulatory exceptions
ensure customer satisfaction and regulatory compliance

name: Exception Escalation and Resolution Process
description: A comprehensive operational workflow governing the management of failed, disputed, and regulatory exception transactions, including their escalation and final resolution.
context: Applies to: Failed transactions (deposits, withdrawals, transfers), Disputed transactions (customer claims unauthorized), Regulatory exceptions (compliance failures, audit issues)

name: Failed Transactions
description: Transactions involving deposits, withdrawals, or transfers that have failed to process correctly and fall within the scope of the exception resolution process.

name: Disputed Transactions
description: Transactions where the customer claims the activity was unauthorized, requiring a dispute resolution workflow.

name: Regulatory Exception Check
description: A compliance gate used to identify and manage failures related to regulatory requirements or audit issues.

name: Transaction Failure Exception Handling Process
description: An operational procedure to manage transactions that were initiated but not completed successfully. It covers various failure types including bank transfers, ATM withdrawals, standing orders, and direct debits, with a resolution SLA of 1–3 business days.
context: Definition: Transaction initiated but not completed successfully

name: Failed Bank Transfer
description: A financial event where a bank transfer was initiated but failed because the recipient account was invalid.

name: Denied ATM Withdrawal
description: A financial event where an ATM withdrawal attempt was denied due to insufficient funds in the account.

name: Failed Standing Order
description: A standing order payment that fails to execute because the associated account has been closed.

name: Rejected Direct Debit
description: A direct debit transaction that is rejected by the system due to insufficient funds available in the account.

name: Impacted Customer
description: The bank customer who is experiencing a high impact because they expected a transaction to complete successfully.
context: Customer Impact: High (customer expecting transaction to complete)

name: Disputed Transactions Process
description: An operational procedure to handle customer claims where a transaction is deemed unauthorized or incorrect. The process carries a high customer impact due to financial loss claims and mandates an investigation window of 5–10 business days.
context: Customer claims transaction unauthorized or incorrect

name: Customer
description: The individual who initiates the dispute by claiming a transaction was unauthorized or incorrect, resulting in a potential financial loss.
context: Customer claims transaction unauthorized or incorrect

name: Disputed Transaction
description: A financial event flagged by the customer as being unauthorized, duplicated, having an incorrect amount, or showing the wrong date.

name: Regulatory Exceptions Remediation Process
description: A process designed to handle operational or compliance issues flagged by audit or risk, such as missing KYC or AML delays. The process aims for remediation within a timeline of 5 to 30 days depending on severity, with potentially low customer impact including account restrictions.
context: Operational or compliance issue flagged by audit/risk

name: Audit and Risk Team
description: The internal body responsible for flagging operational or compliance issues as regulatory exceptions that require remediation.
context: Operational or compliance issue flagged by audit/risk

name: KYC Documentation Completeness Check
description: A compliance gate used to identify if mandatory KYC documentation is missing, which, if failed, triggers a Category 3 Regulatory Exception.

name: AML Screening Timeline Verification
description: A control point to ensure AML screening has been completed within required timeframes; delays are flagged as regulatory exceptions.

name: Transaction Policy Limit Review
description: A check to ensure transactions remain within defined policy limits. Transactions exceeding these limits are flagged as regulatory exceptions.

name: Regulatory Reporting Accuracy Check
description: A mandatory check to ensure regulatory reports are accurate. Errors discovered here are categorized as regulatory exceptions.

name: Account Restriction Trigger
description: A decision point based on the internal operational or compliance issue where the bank determines if a customer account needs to be restricted.
context: Customer Impact: Low (internal issue, may require account restriction)

name: Exception Remediation
description: The action of resolving the flagged regulatory exception within the specified SLA of 5 to 30 days.

name: Exception Detection Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for identifying operational exceptions through automated monitoring of transactions and compliance flags. The process results in the automatic logging of identified issues to an exception queue.

name: Automated Exception Monitoring
description: A discrete stage where the system monitors for failed transactions, unusual patterns, regulatory alerts, and KYC/AML verification issues.

name: Exception Queue Logging
description: The final action in the automated detection sequence where detected exceptions are automatically recorded into the exception queue.
context: Action: Automatic logging to exception queue

name: Automated Monitoring System
description: The system responsible for monitoring logs, fraud rules, and compliance flags to detect exceptions.

name: Failed Transaction
description: A transaction attempt that has failed and is captured via system logs for exception detection.

name: Unusual Transaction Pattern
description: Transactions that trigger fraud rules due to abnormal patterns and are flagged as exceptions.

name: Regulatory Alert Checkpoint
description: A compliance gate where regulatory alerts are flagged, triggering an exception log.

name: KYC/AML Exception Checkpoint
description: A verification gate that identifies issues during the KYC or AML process and logs them as exceptions.

name: Manual Detection Process
description: The operational workflow for identifying and logging exceptions via staff reports, teller observations, audit findings, and regulator communications. The process concludes with escalation to the exception team.
context: Logged by staff, escalated to exception team

name: Staff Reporting Step
description: The collection of reports regarding customer complaints via phone, email, or branch visits to identify potential operational issues.

name: Teller Observation Step
description: The identification of a potential issue based on a teller observing a rejected transaction during processing.

name: Audit Finding Review Step
description: The identification of operational exceptions arising from formal control testing performed during audits.

name: Regulator Communication Review Step
description: The process of receiving and acting upon regulatory exceptions communicated by the regulator.

name: Exception Logging and Escalation Step
description: The final action where the detected exception is logged by staff and formally escalated to the exception team.
context: Action: Logged by staff, escalated to exception team

name: Bank Staff
description: Personnel responsible for reporting complaints, observing transaction failures, and logging exceptions for escalation.

name: Teller
description: Front-line staff responsible for observing and reporting rejected transactions.

name: Exception Team
description: The specialized team to which manual detections are escalated for further handling.

name: Regulator
description: External body that communicates regulatory exceptions to the bank.

name: Complaining Customer
description: The customer who initiates a complaint via phone, email, or branch, triggering the manual detection process.

name: Exception Triage & Categorization Process
description: The initial phase of handling reported exceptions, focusing on the immediate logging of the event, categorization based on exception type, and severity assessment to determine if escalation is required.

name: Exception Logging
description: The immediate recording of an exception including the generation of an Exception ID, timestamp, reporter details, and an initial description of the event.

name: Exception Categorization
description: The process of assigning a category to the exception based on whether it is a failed transaction, customer dispute, or regulatory issue.
context: Is it a failed transaction? → Category 1
Is it a customer dispute? → Category 2

name: Severity Assessment
description: Evaluating the impact of the exception by analyzing the amount involved, the impact on the customer, and regulatory implications.

name: Escalation Trigger Decision
description: A decision point during severity assessment to determine if the exception necessitates further escalation based on the assessed impact and implications.

name: Failed Transaction Investigation Process
description: An operational procedure for investigating failed transactions to determine the cause of failure and implement the appropriate resolution, such as refunds or retries.

name: Transaction Record Retrieval
description: The initial action of pulling the specific transaction record from the banking system to begin the investigation.

name: Failure Status Analysis
description: The process of checking the system status to identify the specific reason why a transaction failed.

name: Customer Authorization Verification
description: A verification step to ensure that the customer had properly authorized the transaction attempt.

name: Account Details Confirmation
description: A check to confirm that the account details associated with the transaction are correct and valid.

name: Reversibility Assessment
description: An assessment to determine if the failed transaction is eligible for reversal based on its current state.

name: Failure Reason Determination
description: A branching point where the investigator identifies the specific failure reason (Insufficient funds, Invalid recipient, Account frozen, or Duplicate prevention) to determine the resolution path.

name: Final Resolution Decision
description: The final decision gate to determine if the outcome should be a refund, a transaction retry, or a customer explanation.
context: Outcome: Refund if funds were debited + failed, retry if appropriate, or explain to customer

name: Failed Transaction
description: The specific financial event that has failed to complete and is the subject of the investigation process.
context: Refund if funds were debited + failed

name: Investigated Account
description: The customer account involved in the failed transaction, which may be checked for balance or freeze status.
context: Confirm balance at time of attempt
Confirm freeze in place and reason

name: Affected Customer
description: The bank customer whose transaction has failed and who must be notified or contacted for correct details.

name: Disputed Transactions Investigation Process
description: An operational workflow for investigating disputed transactions to determine if they were authorized, unauthorized, or require further escalation. The process involves reviewing transaction details, customer history, and negligence factors to determine the refund outcome.

name: Pull Transaction Details
description: The initial action of retrieving the specific details of the transaction under dispute to begin the investigation.

name: Verify Customer Authorization
description: A step to determine whether the customer actually authorized the transaction in question.

name: Verify Timestamp and Amount
description: A technical check of the transaction's timing and monetary value to validate the claim.
context: Timeline: When reported vs. when occurred?

name: Review Customer History and Patterns
description: An analytical review of the customer's previous transaction behavior to identify any patterns that might indicate fraud or normal usage.

name: Assess Fraud Likelihood
description: The final evaluative step where the investigator determines the probability that the transaction was fraudulent based on the collected evidence.

name: Transaction Authorization Decision
description: A decision gate based on the investigation outcome that determines if a transaction is categorized as Unauthorized, Authorized, or Disputed, triggering different response paths.

name: Disputed Transaction
description: The specific financial event being investigated for authorization and fraud likelihood.

name: Complaining Customer
description: The bank customer who is disputing a transaction and whose authorization and negligence (e.g., password sharing) are being assessed.

name: Regulatory Exceptions Investigation Process
description: A workflow designed to identify, assess, and remediate regulatory failures within the bank's operations, ensuring audit trails are maintained and customer impacts are mitigated.

name: Identify Specific Regulatory Issue
description: The initial step in the investigation process where the specific nature of the regulatory breach or exception is determined.

name: Assess Impact
description: Evaluating whether the regulatory exception has a customer-facing impact or is strictly an internal failure.

name: Determine Remediation Steps
description: Deciding upon the specific corrective actions required to resolve the identified regulatory exception.

name: Check for Widespread Impact
description: A review step to determine if the regulatory issue is an isolated incident or if other customers are similarly affected.

name: Document for Audit Trail
description: The final step of the investigation process to ensure all findings and remediation actions are formally recorded for auditing purposes.

name: KYC Documentation Availability Gate
description: A decision point during the remediation of missing KYC where the bank decides whether to proceed with account activity based on the customer's ability to provide missing documents.
context: Obtain missing docs immediately, suspend if can't provide

name: AML Screening Flag Gate
description: A decision point during retroactive AML screening where a result is either resolved or escalated if a flag is generated.

name: KYC Verification Checkpoint
description: A control point verifying that accounts have been opened with the required identity verification documents.

name: AML Screening Timing Checkpoint
description: A control point verifying that AML screening was performed within the required timeframe relative to account opening.

name: Exception Impacted Account
description: Accounts subject to regulatory exceptions, including those with missing KYC, delayed AML screening, or rate errors.

name: Affected Customer
description: The customer subject to the regulatory exception investigation and potential remediation (e.g., receiving back-interest).
context: add back-interest if in customer's favor

name: Failed Transaction Resolution Process
description: An operational workflow to resolve failed transactions through three primary paths: reprocessing, refunding with compensation, or manual facilitation based on the specific failure scenario.

name: Transaction Resolution Path Decision
description: A branching point where staff must determine whether to Reprocess the transaction, provide a Refund + Compensation, or perform Manual Facilitation based on fund availability and customer intent.

name: Transaction Reprocessing Step
description: A sequence of actions to resolve a failure by confirming fund availability, resubmitting the transaction, notifying the customer of success, and closing the exception record.

name: Refund and Compensation Step
description: A remediation sequence triggered when funds were debited despite a transaction failure, involving an immediate refund, interest addition, and potential service failure compensation.
context: If funds were debited despite failure: Refund immediately

name: Manual Transaction Facilitation Step
description: An override procedure used when a customer wishes to proceed despite system blocks, requiring staff to manually facilitate the transaction and document the justification for the override.
context: Customer wants to proceed but system blocks

name: Bank Staff
description: The personnel responsible for executing resolution options, including reprocessing transactions, issuing refunds, and facilitating manual overrides.

name: Bank Customer
description: The recipient of transaction success confirmations, refunds, and apologies, and the party requesting manual facilitation when system blocks occur.
context: Customer wants to proceed but system blocks

name: Failed Transaction
description: A financial event that has failed to complete successfully and requires resolution through the reprocessing, refund, or manual override workflows.
context: If funds were debited despite failure

name: Disputed Transactions Resolution Process
description: An operational workflow for handling customer disputes regarding transactions. The process branches into three distinct resolution paths (Refund, Educate & Retain, or Merchant Escalation) based on the nature of the dispute.

name: Dispute Resolution Path Selection
description: A decision gate to determine whether a disputed transaction should be handled via a direct refund, customer education, or escalation to the merchant/card scheme based on the evidence provided.

name: Refund Execution Step
description: The process of issuing a refund to a customer when unauthorized activity or merchant error is confirmed. This includes a 10 business day timeline for completion, addition of interest if delayed, and a formal apology.
context: Customer proves unauthorized OR Merchant error confirmed

name: Customer Education and Retention Step
description: A step used when a customer authorized a transaction but regrets it. It involves explaining the terms of service and offering the setup of account safeguards such as daily limits and alerts.
context: Offer to set up safeguards (daily limits, alerts)

name: Merchant Dispute Escalation Step
description: The procedure for handling payment disputes via chargeback claims. This involves escalating the matter to the card scheme and initiating a merchant investigation to be resolved according to scheme rules.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who initiates the dispute and provides proof of unauthorized activity or expresses regret over an authorized transaction.

name: Merchant
description: The external entity where merchant errors are confirmed or where investigations are initiated for chargeback claims.

name: Card Scheme
description: The governing body or system to which payment disputes are escalated for resolution according to predefined scheme rules.

name: Disputed Transaction
description: A financial event flagged by the customer as unauthorized, an error, or a point of regret, requiring investigation and resolution.

name: Regulatory Exceptions Resolution Process
description: The operational workflow for handling and resolving regulatory exceptions. It provides three distinct resolution paths based on the nature of the issue: immediate remediation, management escalation, or temporary account restriction.

name: Regulatory Exception Resolution Path Selection
description: A decision gate where the handler determines which of the three resolution options (Option A, B, or C) is appropriate based on the severity and nature of the regulatory issue.

name: Immediate Remediation Execution
description: The process of fixing a regulatory issue immediately by obtaining missing KYC or correcting rates. Includes customer notification, documentation of the fix, and closing the exception.
context: Fix the issue (get missing KYC, correct rate, etc.)

name: Management Escalation for Approval
description: The process of moving an exception to senior management when a management decision is required. This involves obtaining a formal approval and documenting the decision before proceeding.
context: Escalate to Head of Operations or Compliance Head

name: Head of Operations
description: A senior management role responsible for reviewing escalated regulatory exceptions and providing formal approval for approved actions.
context: Escalate to Head of Operations or Compliance Head

name: Compliance Head
description: A senior management role responsible for reviewing escalated regulatory exceptions and providing formal approval for approved actions.
context: Escalate to Head of Operations or Compliance Head

name: Temporary Account Restriction
description: The process applied when a regulatory issue cannot be resolved immediately. It involves placing a hold on transactions and setting a remediation deadline before reactivation.
context: If regulatory issue cannot be immediately resolved

name: Restricted Account
description: A customer account that has been temporarily restricted to prevent transactions due to an unresolved regulatory exception.

name: Affected Customer
description: The customer associated with the regulatory exception who may need to be notified or provide missing information during remediation.

name: Customer Communication Process
description: A procedure for notifying customers regarding the outcome of failed or disputed transactions. It utilizes specific templates to communicate actions taken and provides contact details for further inquiries or escalation.
context: We attempted to process your [transfer/withdrawal] of £[amount] on [date], but it failed

name: Failed Transaction Notification
description: The action of informing a customer that a transfer or withdrawal failed, detailing the reason and the resulting action (Reprocessed, Refunded, or Awaiting action).
context: We attempted to process your [transfer/withdrawal] of £[amount] on [date], but it failed due to [reason].

name: Disputed Transaction Notification
description: The action of communicating the outcome of a transaction dispute investigation to the customer, stating whether the transaction was authorized or unauthorized and the resulting action.
context: Thank you for reporting the disputed transaction of £[amount] on [date].

name: FirstUK Bank Customer Service
description: The department responsible for issuing notifications to customers regarding failed or disputed transactions and serving as the primary point of contact for questions.
context: contact us at 0800-555-2265. Regards, FirstUK Bank Customer Service

name: Customer
description: The bank client who receives notifications regarding transaction failures or dispute outcomes and who may initiate contact or escalate to the Ombudsman.
context: If you disagree with our findings, contact Financial Ombudsman Service.

name: Financial Ombudsman Service
description: The external body the customer is directed to contact if they disagree with the bank's findings regarding a disputed transaction.
context: If you disagree with our findings, contact Financial Ombudsman Service.

name: Failed Transaction
description: A transfer or withdrawal that could not be processed and triggers a customer notification.
context: We attempted to process your [transfer/withdrawal] of £[amount] on [date], but it failed

name: Disputed Transaction
description: A transaction reported by a customer as disputed, which undergoes investigation to determine if it was authorized or unauthorized.
context: Thank you for reporting the disputed transaction of £[amount] on [date].

name: Exception Resolution Quality Assurance Process
description: A quality assurance workflow consisting of post-resolution reviews for individual exceptions and the generation of a Monthly Exception Report to track trends, resolution times, and satisfaction.

name: Post-Resolution Review
description: A discrete review stage performed for each exception to ensure the investigation is documented, the resolution is justified, and the customer has been notified.

name: Refund Processing
description: The action of processing a refund if applicable, which must be completed within the defined Service Level Agreement (SLA).

name: Escalation Documentation
description: The requirement to document a clear reason whenever an exception has been escalated.

name: Monthly Exception Reporting
description: The creation of a monthly report aggregating total exceptions, categories (failed, disputed, regulatory), status, resolution times, and customer satisfaction trends.

name: Refund Applicability Check
description: A decision point to determine if a refund is required as part of the resolution; if so, it triggers the SLA-bound refund process.

name: Escalation Trigger Check
description: A decision point to determine if the case was escalated, necessitating the documentation of a clear reason for the escalation.

name: Customer
description: The subject of the exception resolution who must be notified of the outcome and whose satisfaction is rated in the monthly report.

name: Financial Escalation Process
description: A procedure defining the triggers and approval paths for escalating financial and regulatory issues based on monetary thresholds and risk factors.

name: Immediate Escalation Trigger Check
description: A decision point to determine if an issue requires immediate escalation based on financial amount (>£5,000), regulatory implications, customer complaints, third-party involvement, or media concern.

name: Approval Level Determination
description: A branching logic that assigns the required approval authority based on the specific financial amount of the transaction or the nature of the regulatory risk.

name: Level 1 — Operations Manager Approval
description: The first tier of escalation for financial amounts less than £1,000, requiring approval from the Operations Manager.

name: Level 2 — Director Approval
description: The second tier of escalation for financial amounts between £1,000 and £5,000, requiring Director level approval.

name: Level 3 — Executive Approval
description: The highest financial escalation tier for amounts exceeding £5,000, requiring approval from the Executive level.

name: Regulatory Tier — Compliance Head Approval
description: A specialized escalation path for issues with regulatory implications, requiring approval from the Compliance Head.

name: Operations Manager
description: The actor responsible for approving escalations where the financial amount is less than £1,000.

name: Director
description: The actor responsible for approving escalations for financial amounts between £1,000 and £5,000.

name: Executive
description: The actor responsible for approving high-value escalations exceeding £5,000.

name: Compliance Head
description: The actor responsible for approving escalations involving regulatory implications.

name: Failed Transfer — Insufficient Funds Resolution Process
description: The operational procedure for handling and resolving failed fund transfers caused by insufficient account balances. It involves investigation of the balance at the time of transaction and customer notification within a 1 business day SLA.
context: Exception: Customer attempted £5,000 transfer, balance only £3,000

name: Balance Confirmation Investigation
description: The step where the bank confirms the exact account balance available at the specific time the transaction was attempted to verify the cause of the failure.
context: Investigation: Confirmed balance at transaction time

name: Customer Notification and Retry Offer
description: The final resolution step where the staff explains the failure to the customer and provides the option to retry the transfer once the necessary funds are available.
context: Resolution: Explain to customer, offer retry once funds available

name: Bank Staff
description: The unnamed bank employee responsible for investigating the balance, notifying the customer, and offering a retry of the transaction.
context: Investigation: Confirmed balance at transaction time

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who attempted the transfer and receives the notification regarding the insufficient funds.

name: Failed Transfer Transaction
description: A specific financial event where a transfer (e.g., £5,000) failed to execute because the available balance (e.g., £3,000) was insufficient.

name: Disputed Standing Order Process
description: An operational workflow to handle exceptions where a customer claims a standing order is unauthorized. The process involves investigation and resolution within a 2 business day SLA.
context: Exception: Customer claims unauthorized standing order to "Unknown Recipient"

name: Bank Staff
description: The implicit actor responsible for investigating the disputed standing order and educating the customer on the resolution.
context: Resolution: Educate customer on standing order setup

name: Complaining Customer
description: The bank customer who has raised a dispute claiming a standing order to an 'Unknown Recipient' was unauthorized.
context: Customer claims unauthorized standing order to "Unknown Recipient"
Educate customer on standing order setup

name: Unauthorized Standing Order Investigation
description: The stage where the bank investigates the claim of an unauthorized standing order to verify the legitimacy of the recipient.
context: Investigation: Found legitimate standing order to Mortgage Company (customer's mortgage)

name: Customer Education and Resolution
description: The final step where the customer is educated on how standing orders are set up and how to view them via online banking.
context: Resolution: Educate customer on standing order setup, explain visibility in online banking

name: Disputed Mortgage Standing Order
description: A specific standing order initially flagged by the customer as unauthorized but found to be a legitimate payment to the customer's mortgage company.
context: Found legitimate standing order to Mortgage Company (customer's mortgage)

name: Standing Order Legitimacy Check
description: A decision point during investigation to determine if the standing order is indeed unauthorized or a legitimate payment.
context: Investigation: Found legitimate standing order to Mortgage Company

name: Duplicate Charge Exception Handling Process
description: An operational workflow to resolve instances where a customer is charged twice for the same transfer due to a failure in system duplicate prevention. The process involves investigation, refunding the duplicate charge with interest and goodwill compensation, and adheres to a 3-business day SLA.
context: Exception: Customer charged twice for £500 transfer

name: Duplicate Transaction Investigation
description: The analysis phase where the system is checked for identical transactions occurring within a short timeframe (1 minute) to confirm a failure in duplicate prevention.
context: Investigation: Two identical transactions within 1 minute (system duplicate prevention failed)

name: Refund and Compensation Execution
description: The final resolution step requiring the refund of the second charge, addition of interest, and the application of a £50 goodwill compensation payment.
context: Resolution: Refund second charge + interest + £50 goodwill compensation

name: Duplicate Prevention System
description: The automated system responsible for preventing duplicate transactions, which in this instance failed to block two identical transfers.

name: Affected Customer
description: The bank customer who has been erroneously charged twice for a single transfer and is the recipient of the refund and compensation.

name: Duplicate Transfer Transaction
description: The financial events consisting of two identical £500 transfers occurring within one minute of each other.

name: Missing KYC Documentation Resolution Process
aliases: Exception: Account opened without identity verification
description: An operational workflow triggered by an audit finding where an account was opened online without identity verification. The process involves investigating the missing KYC file and requesting documentation from the customer within a 5-day SLA.
context: Exception: Account opened without identity verification (audit finding)
Investigation: KYC file missing; customer opened via online
Resolution: Email customer, request identity document immediately

name: KYC File Investigation
description: The initial stage of the exception process where the missing nature of the KYC file is confirmed and the account opening channel (online) is identified.
context: Investigation: KYC file missing; customer opened via online

name: Customer Documentation Request
description: The action of contacting the customer via email to immediately request the missing identity documents required for KYC compliance.
context: Resolution: Email customer, request identity document immediately

name: Identity Document Provision Check
description: A decision gate based on a 5-day SLA to determine if the customer has provided the required identity documents. If the document is not provided, the account must be restricted.
context: SLA: 5 days (account restricted if doc not provided)

name: Identity Verification Compliance Gate
description: The mandatory regulatory control point ensuring that identity verification is completed for accounts opened via online channels to satisfy audit requirements.
context: Account opened without identity verification (audit finding)

name: Operations Analyst
description: The staff member responsible for performing the investigation, emailing the customer, and enforcing the account restriction if the SLA is breached.
context: Resolution: Email customer, request identity document immediately

name: Online Applicant
description: The customer who opened an account via the online channel and is currently missing required identity documentation.
context: Email customer, request identity document immediately

name: Unverified Online Account
description: The specific bank account subject to an audit finding for missing KYC, which is liable to be restricted if documentation is not provided within 5 days.
context: account restricted if doc not provided

name: Identity Document
description: The official identity documentation required to resolve the audit exception and satisfy the KYC file requirement.

name: Head of Operations
description: Senior operational leader responsible for the final sign-off and approval of the operational procedure document.

name: Head of Compliance
description: Senior compliance leader responsible for the final sign-off and approval of the operational procedure document to ensure regulatory alignment.
